dedupe_keys.name: guidelines for evaluating internet access resilience in canada v1 0 cfdir september 2023

description: These guidelines from the Canadian Forum for Digital Infrastructure Resilience set out how home users, remote workers, small businesses, enterprises and internet service providers can evaluate and increase the resilience of internet access. They define internet access resilience and work through scenarios (internet access at home, for remote workers and further user types), each with a resilience objective, an outage tolerance and recommendations, motivated by the Canada-wide Rogers network outage of July 2022. Producer: the Internet Resilience Working Group of CFDIR, published as version 1.0 on 8 September 2023 (39 pages). Coverage: Canada. Access: free PDF on the Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada site. Licence and cost: free; the document is marked TLP:CLEAR, distributable without restriction with acknowledgement. Caveats: guidance text with no measured outage data, and version 1.0 may have been superseded. Simulation uses: the scenarios and outage tolerance definitions give ready-made assumptions for resilience and emergency-response studies of access networks. Related records: none linked.
